import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_2.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']

# Step 2: Join the tables to form the target schema
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Join df1 and df0 on 'movie_id' to get 'title' for each rating record
df1_0 = pd.merge(df1, df0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Join the above result with df2 on 'user_id' to get 'age' and 'occupation'
df_final = pd.merge(df1_0, df2[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Step 3: Ensure correct data types according to target schema
# 'title': string
df_final['title'] = df_final['title'].astype(str)

# 'user_id': float
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(float)

# 'movie_id': integer
df_final['movie_id'] = df_final['movie_id'].astype(int)

# 'rating': float
df_final['rating'] = df_final['rating'].astype(float)

# 'timestamp': float
df_final['timestamp'] = df_final['timestamp'].astype(float)

# 'age': float
df_final['age'] = df_final['age'].astype(float)

# 'occupation': float
df_final['occupation'] = df_final['occupation'].astype(float)

# Step 4: Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_final[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Step 5: Write the result to the specified output CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 with the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by title, user_id, movie_id and aggregate other columns by mean
result = joined_all.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Ensure column order and types match target schema
result = result[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
